_comment: LOCKSTEP prefixes: template paths that MUST stay byte-identical to a deployed vault. A governed change edits the repo's vault-template/<prefix>/...; the post-merge mirror copies it into the live vault; this manifest lets template-parity.py prove the mirror is complete. The dividing line is GOVERNANCE CONTENT vs PER-INSTANCE CONFIGURATION: lockstep covers the INV-3 scaffold (99-Operations/scripts/, 99-Operations/schemas/), the spec-as-code runbooks (96-Runbooks/) and the agent commands that carry ceremony (.claude/commands/) -- artifacts that are single-source-of-truth by their own definition, where an instance edit is a governance fork rather than local ownership. Everything NOT under a lockstep prefix is SEED (seeded once at deploy, then owned/edited per instance: CLAUDE.md, config, 40-Treasury/, Catalog indexes, README, .claude/settings.json) and is deliberately not compared. Matching is directory-prefix, so any file under a prefix in EITHER tree is compared and a newly-shipped file cannot go silently unchecked.
_seed_comment: .claude/ is NOT wholly lockstep. Only .claude/commands/ is. `.claude/settings.json` stays SEED deliberately -- it carries per-instance permissions, sandbox scope and HOOK REGISTRATION. Consequence, stated rather than discovered: because settings.json is never compared, hook REGISTRATION cannot be verified by parity at all. A hook can be deployed, byte-correct and never loaded while this check reports zero drift. That gap needs an assertion, not a comparison, and is out of scope here (platform hardening item 32).
_exclude_comment: Files under a lockstep prefix that legitimately diverge because the live vault GENERATES them (the template ships the generator, not its output). Deliberate duplication per the operation's standing list — do not rationalize. naming-rules.json is emitted into the live vault by vault_naming.py.
_bin_comment: 99-Operations/bin/ is DELIBERATELY NOT a lockstep prefix. It holds RENDER OUTPUT whose single source is 99-Operations/scripts/, which IS lockstep - the template ships the generator, not its output. Same category as the naming-rules.json exclusion below. Adding it would also fail permanently: the comparator returns an empty set for an absent directory and vault-template/ ships no bin/, so parity would report one drift per fleet member, forever, and a check that is always red is a check nobody reads. The division of labour: PARITY compares hand-maintained scaffold; RENDER/RECONCILE compares generated output against the note that produced it. Neither substitutes for the other, and 99-Operations/bin/ is reconcile's jurisdiction. It is also git-ignored in both trees - see .gitignore.
